rows.reply: The innkeeper sets down two mugs of cider and asks how the road was. A fire crackles in the hearth.
The market is busy and cheerful. A baker offers Max a free roll to try, smiling.
Arin laughs at the joke and hands Max the map. 'You lead, then,' she says.
From the ridge the valley spreads out green and quiet under a clear sky.
A light rain starts. Max's cloak is damp by the time they reach the bridge, nothing worse.
The ferryman wants a silver more than last week. 'Prices went up,' he shrugs.
A strap on Max's pack snaps; it takes a few minutes to knot it back together.
The clerk is curt with Max and makes him wait at the back of the line.
The trail they followed ends at a washed-out gully. They will lose half a day going around.
When Max reaches for his purse it is gone; a boy is already disappearing into the crowd.
The captain refuses Max passage outright. 'No papers, no ship.' The door shuts.
Max lands badly jumping the ditch and his ankle swells; walking will be slow for days.
Arrows hiss out of the trees. One takes Max's horse in the neck and it goes down screaming.
They return to find the safehouse burning. Every supply and letter they left there is ash.
Guards close in from both ends of the alley. Arin is seized and dragged away before Max can reach her.
The blade opens Max's side. Blood soaks his shirt and the world tilts as he staggers.
Old Bren falls and does not get up. The man who raised Max is dead on the cobbles.
The council hears the forged letters and brands Max a traitor. His name, lands and rank are stripped before nightfall.
The gates break. Smoke rises over the whole city Max swore to defend, and the defenders run.
The ritual completes. Max feels the curse settle into his bones; the healer says it cannot be lifted.
